title: test(console): wait for the public-client lookup before counting it (objectui#12344)
body:
Fixes #12344
Clause-②: no

## What

`OAuthConsentPage.public-client-12301.test.tsx`, case "shows neither a name nor the id while the lookup is in flight": the lookup call count is now awaited instead of read the moment the placeholder text appears.

- `expect(lookupCalls(fetchMock)).toHaveLength(1)` → `await waitFor(() => expect(lookupCalls(fetchMock)).toHaveLength(1))`.
- The in-flight reads are kept as written (no alert, the client id drawn nowhere).
- After them the case re-asserts the count is still 1, so "the page asks once" stays pinned in this case.

Why: the placeholder is drawn by the commit; the public-client `fetch` is started in the passive `useEffect` that runs after it. `findByText` can resolve between the two, and the count then reads 0. This is the CI failure on run 38489613706 (shard 9/12): `expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0`.

Sweep of the file's other cases for the same "text appears, then count calls" ordering:
- "asks the served route…" counts after `Acme Notes wants to access your account` is drawn. That text exists only after the lookup has answered, so the call has already happened. No race.
- "does not ask the session-required route for a signed-out visitor" asserts zero calls after `login-stub`. The effect is gated on a signed-in user id and the user is null, so there is no pending call to race.
- The four could-not-identify cases count no calls.

Test file only, plus an empty-frontmatter changeset. No skip, retry, quarantine or timeout change.

## Evidence (head 5a741ad21)

- **Deterministic reproduction.** A local-only probe deferred the page effect's `fetch` by 50 ms (`setTimeout`), landed with the anchor-must-hit ablation tool and restored by a trap. Both legs ran in the same run:
  - Old assertion with the probe: `Tests 1 failed | 7 passed (8)`, the CI message exactly: `AssertionError: expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0`.
  - New assertion with the probe: `Tests 8 passed (8)`.
  - Restore proved by blob-hash match with HEAD on both files and an empty `git diff HEAD`. The probe is not committed.
- **The file 20 times in a row** (repo-root `pnpm exec vitest run FILE`, one process per run): 20 of 20 runs exit 0, `Tests 8 passed (8)` each.
- **`apps/console/src/pages/auth/`**: `Test Files 15 passed (15)`, `Tests 87 passed (87)`, exit 0.
- **Type-check, narrowed and declared.** The console closure (35 workspace packages, no `dist/` in this container) was not built, so the full `type-check` was NOT run; CI runs it.
  - What ran instead: `tsc --noEmit` on the test file, with the console tsconfig, at head and with the base test file in its place.
  - Both runs give the same 5 errors, all TS2307 for unbuilt `@object-ui/*` packages. No error is on a line this diff touches.
- **Lint narrowed to the file**: `eslint --no-inline-config FILE` exit 0; `--format json` gives 1 file, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
  - This is the narrowed form of `pnpm lint`. The console package's `lint` script is `eslint .`, and the repo-wide run belongs to CI.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-fixed.mjs` exit 0; `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` exit 0 (one empty-frontmatter changeset).
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: 0 new citations, exit 0.

## Acceptance notes

- A2 boundary: the trailing count assertion catches a second lookup that has started by the time the in-flight reads finish. A later stray call would land after the case ends. The first case's `toEqual([expected])`, read after the answer, also pins one call.
